catalogue_metadata.title: AuditSphere Educational Selected Annex A Controls Catalogue
catalogue_metadata.description: An educational subset of 20 selected Annex A controls representing all four ISO/IEC 27001:2022 themes (Organizational, People, Physical, Technological). Paraphrased for educational and portfolio evaluation purposes.
catalogue_metadata.disclaimer: This catalogue is an educational subset of ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A controls and does not constitute a complete Statement of Applicability or certification audit checklist.

controls.title: Policies for Information Security
controls.description: Information security policies and topic-specific policies must be defined, endorsed by executive leadership, published, communicated across the organization, and reviewed periodically or upon significant operational changes.
controls.objective: Provide management direction and support for information security in accordance with business requirements and relevant laws.
assessment_questions: Is there an overarching information security policy approved by executive management?
Are topic-specific policies (e.g., access control, backup, data protection) documented and disseminated?
Is there an established schedule for regular review and maintenance of security policies?
suggested_evidence: Approved Information Security Policy document
Executive approval sign-off or committee minutes
Policy review schedule and change log
Staff acknowledgment records
example_gaps: Information security policy has not been reviewed or updated for over 24 months.
Topic-specific policies lack documented executive leadership approval.
example_recommendations: Establish an annual policy review cadence approved by the ISMS steering committee.
Formally document executive sign-off and communicate updated policies to all personnel.

controls.title: Access Control
controls.description: Rules to control physical and logical access to information and associated assets must be established, documented, and enforced based on business and security prerequisites.
controls.objective: Ensure authorized access and prevent unauthorized access to systems, data, and business networks.
assessment_questions: Does a formalized access control policy exist outlining principles like least privilege and need-to-know?
Are user access requests subject to formal business justification and owner approval?
Is remote access governed by stringent access control guidelines?
suggested_evidence: Documented Access Control Policy
Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) matrix
User access request tickets with owner sign-off
example_gaps: Access is granted on verbal request without written system-owner authorization.
Role-based access matrix is missing or poorly defined for core administrative systems.
example_recommendations: Institute a ticketing workflow requiring documented owner approval for all access requests.
Define and publish an enterprise Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) schema.

controls.title: Access Rights Management
controls.description: The allocation, modification, and revocation of access rights to information assets must be systematically provisioned, altered, and removed in accordance with access control rules and employment lifecycle events.
controls.objective: Ensure access rights remain aligned with current job roles and are promptly revoked upon transfer or separation.
assessment_questions: Are user access reviews conducted at regular intervals (e.g., quarterly or biannually)?
Is there a verified de-provisioning process that immediately disables accounts upon employee termination?
Are dormant or orphan accounts routinely identified and disabled?
suggested_evidence: Periodic user access review reports and sign-offs
HR termination notification timestamps matched against directory disablement logs
Automated de-provisioning workflow configurations
example_gaps: Terminated contractor accounts remained active for weeks following contract conclusion.
Access reviews are not formally tracked or documented with system-owner approvals.
example_recommendations: Integrate HR offboarding notifications with identity provider (IdP) for immediate account suspension.
Mandate quarterly access re-certifications across critical production environments.

controls.title: Information Security Incident Management Planning
controls.description: The organization must plan and prepare for managing security incidents by defining incident processes, roles, responsibilities, reporting hierarchies, and coordination channels.
controls.objective: Ensure effective and timely response to security events and operational incidents.
assessment_questions: Is there a documented incident response plan with clearly designated incident roles and escalations?
Are communication pathways defined for internal teams, legal advisors, regulators, and affected clients?
Is the incident response plan tested periodically via tabletop exercises or simulated drills?
suggested_evidence: Incident Response Plan (IRP) documentation
Call tree / contact escalation registry
Tabletop simulation summary report and action items
example_gaps: Incident response plan exists on paper but has never been tested in simulated exercises.
Escalation contact lists are out of date and contain departed staff members.
example_recommendations: Schedule and execute an annual tabletop simulation exercise involving technical and executive leads.
Establish a quarterly cadence to verify and update incident response call rosters.

controls.title: Legal, Statutory, Regulatory and Contractual Requirements
controls.description: Legal, statutory, regulatory, and contractual requirements relevant to information security, and the organization's approach to satisfy them, must be explicitly documented, updated, and adhered to.
controls.objective: Prevent breaches of legal, regulatory, or contractual obligations related to information security.
assessment_questions: Is a comprehensive legal and compliance register maintained and updated regularly?
Are contractual cybersecurity and audit commitments tracked for critical client and partner agreements?
Are data sovereignty and intellectual property obligations systematically monitored?
suggested_evidence: Legal and Regulatory Compliance Register
Customer Data Protection Agreements (DPAs)
Internal compliance audit reports
example_gaps: Compliance register has not incorporated recent regional data privacy regulatory amendments.
No formal process exists to review security commitments made in customized client contracts.
example_recommendations: Perform a comprehensive review with legal counsel to update the regulatory obligations register.
Create a contract review checklist ensuring security clauses align with operational capabilities.

controls.title: Privacy and Protection of Personally Identifiable Information
controls.description: The organization must identify and implement technical and organizational controls to protect personally identifiable information (PII) according to relevant privacy laws and regulations.
controls.objective: Ensure compliance with data protection laws and safeguard personal data belonging to customers and staff.
assessment_questions: Is PII classified and mapped across data processing workflows and technical repositories?
Are Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) conducted before deploying new data processing systems?
Are data subject access and deletion request procedures implemented and operational?
suggested_evidence: Record of Processing Activities (ROPA)
Completed DPIA assessments
Data subject rights request workflow documentation
Privacy Notice
example_gaps: No structured Record of Processing Activities (ROPA) exists to track customer PII flows.
Data retention timelines for customer personal data are neither defined nor automated.
example_recommendations: Compile and maintain a formal Data Flow and Record of Processing Activities inventory.
Implement automated data retention and purge routines for expired personal records.

controls.title: Personnel Screening
controls.description: Background verification checks on all candidates for employment, contractors, and relevant third-party personnel must be carried out prior to joining in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, and ethics.
controls.objective: Verify that all personnel are suitable and trustworthy for their intended roles.
assessment_questions: Are pre-employment background checks mandated for all permanent and contract personnel?
Are enhanced screening procedures (e.g., criminal history, credit) conducted for high-privilege roles?
Are screening records stored securely with appropriate privacy protections?
suggested_evidence: Pre-employment Screening Policy
Sample completed background check confirmation files (anonymized)
Contractor onboarding checklist
example_gaps: Background screening is enforced for full-time employees but skipped for third-party contractors.
High-privilege system administrators are not subjected to enhanced financial or criminal background checks.
example_recommendations: Standardize background screening requirements across all contractor and vendor staffing agreements.
Implement risk-based enhanced vetting for personnel granted root or domain-admin privileges.

controls.title: Information Security Awareness, Education and Training
controls.description: Personnel and relevant contractors must receive appropriate security awareness education, training, and regular updates relevant to their organizational roles.
controls.objective: Ensure personnel understand information security responsibilities and maintain situational awareness.
assessment_questions: Is security awareness training mandatory for all new hires during onboarding?
Is refresher security training delivered at least annually to all staff?
Are simulated phishing campaigns executed to measure workforce vigilance?
suggested_evidence: Security awareness training curriculum and slides
LMS completion records demonstrating 95%+ participation
Simulated phishing exercise metric reports
example_gaps: Security awareness training is conducted at orientation but never refreshed annually.
No remediation training is provided to personnel who fail simulated phishing assessments.
example_recommendations: Deploy mandatory annual refresher training with automated tracking and managerial escalation.
Provide immediate micro-learning modules for individuals who click simulated phishing links.

controls.title: Confidentiality or Non-Disclosure Agreements
controls.description: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements reflecting the organization's requirements for protection of information must be identified, documented, regularly reviewed, and signed by personnel and third parties.
controls.objective: Protect proprietary and sensitive information through legally enforceable confidentiality agreements.
assessment_questions: Do all employment agreements incorporate binding confidentiality and IP protection clauses?
Are NDAs executed with third-party vendors and contractors prior to sharing confidential data?
Do confidentiality obligations explicitly survive termination of employment or engagement?
suggested_evidence: Standard employee confidentiality agreement template
Sample executed employee NDAs
Third-party Non-Disclosure Agreement repository
example_gaps: Contractor agreements lack explicit clauses stating that confidentiality duties persist post-termination.
NDAs with prospective business partners are executed inconsistently.
example_recommendations: Review and update standard employment and contractor templates to ensure post-employment confidentiality clauses.
Establish a centralized repository and pre-engagement NDA gatekeeper in procurement.

controls.title: Information Security Event Reporting
controls.description: The organization must provide a clear mechanism for personnel to report observed or suspected information security events in a timely and frictionless manner.
controls.objective: Ensure security events are communicated rapidly to enable timely investigation and containment.
assessment_questions: Is there an easily accessible, well-known channel (e.g., dedicated email, portal button) for reporting security events?
Are employees trained on what constitutes a reportable security event vs an IT bug?
Is there a policy protecting whistleblowers or employees reporting incidents in good faith?
suggested_evidence: Incident reporting procedure guide
Intranet incident reporting button / ticketing queue
Log of employee-reported security observations
example_gaps: Employees lack a dedicated incident reporting channel and report security issues via casual chat channels.
Staff members are hesitant to report accidental data leaks due to fear of punitive reprisals.
example_recommendations: Publish a prominent 'Report Security Event' link on the corporate portal with clear SLA commitments.
Adopt a blameless reporting culture policy that encourages rapid disclosure of security incidents.

controls.title: Physical Security Perimeters
controls.description: Security perimeters must be defined and used to protect areas that contain information and other associated assets, including data centers, server closets, and sensitive corporate offices.
controls.objective: Prevent unauthorized physical access, damage, and interference to the organization’s information facilities.
assessment_questions: Are physical security perimeters established around server rooms and sensitive operational areas?
Are perimeter barriers (doors, walls, gates) structurally sound and resistant to forced entry?
Are security boundary perimeters clearly designated and segregated from public access areas?
suggested_evidence: Facility floor plans showing security perimeters and secure zones
Physical security risk assessment report
Access barrier inspection logs
example_gaps: Server room partitions stop at the false ceiling level, permitting crawlspace physical bypass.
Office reception area lacks physical separation from employee work areas and executive suites.
example_recommendations: Extend physical security slab-to-slab barriers to enclose secure server infrastructure.
Install access-controlled turnstiles or secured internal doors dividing visitor zones from operations.

controls.title: Physical Entry Controls
controls.description: Secure areas must be protected by appropriate entry controls to ensure that only authorized personnel are allowed access, with visitors escorted and recorded.
controls.objective: Control and record entry to secure areas to prevent unauthorized physical tampering or theft.
assessment_questions: Is electronic badge access enforced at all exterior doors and interior high-security rooms?
Are visitors required to present government photo ID, sign a visitor log, and wear visitor badges?
Are visitor access logs audited and retained for an appropriate compliance period?
suggested_evidence: Electronic access control system badge swipe logs
Visitor sign-in register / digital visitor management export
Visitor badge policy and escort guidelines
example_gaps: Tailgating / piggybacking through secure perimeter doors is common during morning rush hours.
Server room visitor log is kept on an unmonitored paper sheet with missing entries.
example_recommendations: Deploy anti-tailgating doors or turnstiles coupled with security guard awareness campaigns.
Transition to a digital visitor management kiosk integrated with automated visitor badge printing.

controls.title: Physical Security Monitoring
controls.description: Premises must be continuously monitored by surveillance systems, intrusion detection systems, or physical patrols to deter and detect unauthorized physical entry.
controls.objective: Detect unauthorized physical intrusion and maintain evidentiary surveillance records.
assessment_questions: Are CCTV cameras positioned at all perimeter entrance and exit points and data center aisles?
Are surveillance video recordings retained for at least 30 to 90 days in a tamper-resistant format?
Are motion detectors and intrusion alarm systems configured to alert on-call security personnel?
suggested_evidence: CCTV camera layout diagram
Video recording retention setting screenshot and archive verification
Intrusion alarm testing logs and alert dispatch records
example_gaps: CCTV camera overlooking the primary backup storage rack has been offline for three weeks.
Surveillance footage is overwritten after only 14 days due to inadequate local storage capacity.
example_recommendations: Implement automated health monitoring for CCTV recording feeds to generate immediate downtime alerts.
Expand network storage capacity to guarantee a minimum 90-day video retention period.

controls.title: Clear Desk and Clear Screen
controls.description: Clear desk rules for papers and removable storage media and clear screen rules for information processing facilities must be defined, communicated, and systematically enforced.
controls.objective: Prevent unauthorized viewing, theft, and loss of papers, media, and screen displays.
assessment_questions: Is an automated screen lock enforced across all workstations after a maximum of 5 to 15 minutes of inactivity?
Are lockable storage cabinets provided to personnel for securing confidential paperwork and keys?
Are periodic physical spot-checks performed outside business hours to verify clear desk adherence?
suggested_evidence: Group Policy / MDM workstation automatic screen lock configuration
Clear Desk and Clear Screen policy document
After-hours physical audit sweep logs
example_gaps: Workstations in open-plan areas do not have automatic screen timeouts enforced by centralized policy.
Sensitive customer payroll printouts were found unattended on shared office printers overnight.
example_recommendations: Enforce a mandatory 10-minute inactivity screen lock via centralized Mobile Device Management (MDM).
Deploy 'Follow-Me' secure badge-release printing so documents only print when the user is present.

controls.title: Privileged Access Rights
controls.description: The allocation and use of privileged access rights must be restricted and controlled through a formal authorization process, dedicated accounts, and privileged access management (PAM) principles.
controls.objective: Prevent misuse and compromise of elevated administrative rights on critical infrastructure.
assessment_questions: Are administrative privileges separated from daily standard user accounts (no admin browsing or email)?
Is Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) strictly enforced on all privileged accounts and bastions?
Is Privileged Access Management (PAM) or just-in-time privilege elevation implemented?
suggested_evidence: Inventory of privileged accounts across domains and cloud tenants
Privileged Access Management (PAM) session recording and vault policy
MFA enforcement policy screenshot on administrative portals
example_gaps: System administrators use shared root or generic domain-admin accounts for everyday tasks.
Privileged cloud console access does not require hardware token or phishing-resistant MFA.
example_recommendations: Mandate individual named administrative accounts and prohibit generic root credentials.
Implement a PAM solution providing session auditing and Just-In-Time (JIT) privilege elevation.

controls.title: Secure Authentication
controls.description: Secure authentication technologies and procedures must be implemented based on information access restrictions and the specific risk profile of the application or service.
controls.objective: Authenticate users and systems reliably to prevent credential stuffing, brute force, and spoofing.
assessment_questions: Is Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) enforced for all employees across corporate SaaS and VPN endpoints?
Are password complexity, length (e.g., 14+ characters), and breach-compromised password screening enforced?
Are single sign-on (SSO) integrations utilized to centralize authentication governance?
suggested_evidence: IdP conditional access policies enforcing MFA for all users
Password policy configuration report from active directory or identity provider
SSO federated application inventory
example_gaps: Legacy enterprise applications still allow single-factor password-only access from untrusted networks.
Account lockout after successive failed login attempts is not configured on public web services.
example_recommendations: Enforce modern adaptive MFA across all corporate web applications and VPN gateways.
Configure automated lockout thresholds and rate-limiting to mitigate brute force attacks.

controls.title: Management of Technical Vulnerabilities
controls.description: Information about technical vulnerabilities of information systems in use must be obtained, the organization's exposure evaluated, and appropriate remediation or patching measures taken.
controls.objective: Prevent the exploitation of known technical software and firmware vulnerabilities.
assessment_questions: Are automated vulnerability scans executed on external and internal assets at least monthly?
Is there a defined patching SLA based on Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) severities?
Are third-party software dependencies and libraries scanned for known CVEs?
suggested_evidence: Vulnerability scanning tool configuration and recent executive summary report
Vulnerability Remediation Policy showing SLA timelines (e.g., Critical within 14 days)
Patch management deployment verification reports
example_gaps: Critical CVSS 9.0+ vulnerabilities remain unpatched on production servers past established SLA limits.
No automated tool is used to monitor software dependency vulnerabilities in custom code.
example_recommendations: Establish an automated vulnerability scanning and patch management cycle with strict SLA enforcement.
Integrate Software Composition Analysis (SCA) into the CI/CD pipeline to flag vulnerable dependencies.

controls.title: Information Backup
controls.description: Backup copies of information, software, and system images must be maintained and regularly tested in accordance with the agreed topic-specific policy on backup.
controls.objective: Protect against data loss, ransomware, and system corruption through reliable, recoverable backups.
assessment_questions: Are automated backups performed daily for critical databases and file repositories?
Are backups stored in an isolated, immutable, or off-site location protected against ransomware?
Are backup restoration procedures tested and documented at least quarterly or annually?
suggested_evidence: Backup policy defining RTO and RPO targets
Automated backup job success dashboards and error alerts
Formal backup restoration drill report with measured recovery times
example_gaps: Backups run automatically, but restoration drills have not been performed in over a year.
Backup repositories share the same active directory domain, exposing them to ransomware destruction.
example_recommendations: Institute quarterly backup restoration tests with documented RTO/RPO validation.
Implement immutable write-once-read-many (WORM) storage or cloud air-gapped backup vaults.

controls.title: Logging
controls.description: Logs that record activities, exceptions, faults, and other relevant events must be produced, stored, protected from tampering, and regularly analyzed.
controls.objective: Record system events to facilitate security investigations, anomaly detection, and operational integrity.
assessment_questions: Are audit logs enabled across operating systems, firewalls, identity providers, and critical databases?
Are security logs forwarded to a centralized SIEM or log repository in real time?
Are log repositories secured with append-only access to prevent administrator tampering or deletion?
suggested_evidence: Centralized SIEM ingestion architecture and retention settings (e.g., 365 days)
Audit logging configuration screenshots from cloud consoles and directory services
Alerting rules configured for suspicious administrative activities
example_gaps: Authentication logs are stored only on local server disks with no centralized forwarding.
System administrators have full permissions to truncate or disable audit logs on servers.
example_recommendations: Deploy a centralized SIEM to aggregate event logs in real time from all network and cloud assets.
Restrict log repository access using write-once permissions to safeguard forensic evidence integrity.

controls.title: Use of Cryptography
controls.description: Rules for the effective use of cryptography, including cryptographic key management, must be defined, approved, and implemented across data in transit and at rest.
controls.objective: Ensure proper and effective use of encryption to protect the confidentiality and integrity of information.
assessment_questions: Is encryption enforced for sensitive data in transit using modern TLS (v1.2+ or v1.3)?
Is encryption at rest enforced across all laptops, databases, and cloud storage volumes?
Is there a formal key management lifecycle covering generation, rotation, storage, and retirement?
suggested_evidence: Cryptographic Standard and Key Management Policy
TLS configuration cipher suite reports on public endpoints (e.g., Qualys SSL Labs A grade)
Full-disk encryption (BitLocker / FileVault) compliance reports from endpoint management
example_gaps: Internal microservice communications utilize unencrypted plaintext HTTP.
Cryptographic keys and API secrets are hardcoded in source code repositories.
example_recommendations: Enforce TLS 1.3 across all external and internal service-to-service communication paths.
Transition all cryptographic keys and credentials to an automated cloud key vault with periodic rotation.
